sections.h2: Where is the Franklin County, TN Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is at 1 South Jefferson Street in Winchester, TN 37398, the county seat, and the phone number is (931) 967-2840. Nancy K. Ringer is listed as the Register, and the office shares the courthouse address with the county's assessor and trustee.

The register's website describes the job in broad terms. The office makes and keeps a record of every instrument the law requires or allows to be filed, from deeds, mortgages, liens and plats to leases, wills, court orders and military discharges. Those records give public notice of who owns land and what claims sit against it, and the papers must stay in the office in the county seat.

For a house sale, that means the deed that moves title to your buyer will be indexed in Winchester, and so will the paper that releases your old loan.

sections.h2: Which Franklin County offices does a seller deal with?
sections.html:
Three offices sit within the same building at 1 South Jefferson Street, so most of a seller's errands can be done in one trip. The register records, the assessor values, and the trustee collects the tax.

Franklin County offices at the Winchester courthouse
OfficeRole in a salePhone
Register of DeedsRecords the deed and releases(931) 967-2840
Property Assessor (Room 101)Appraises and assesses each parcel(931) 967-3869
Trustee (P.O. Box 340)Collects property tax(931) 967-2962

Source: Franklin County Property Assessor, Franklin County Trustee and the Register of Deeds site. The assessor's hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The assessor's office keeps an individual property record card on every parcel in the county, about 25,000 in all. Records are updated weekly through the state's Local Assessor System for web viewing, and a public terminal at the office can pull them up. Ask the staff to confirm the owner of record and the classification before you set a price.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax on a Franklin County home sale?
sections.html:
The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of price or value on a transfer of real property, collected by the register from the buyer. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimate for the median owner-occupied home in Franklin County is $236,900, and the tax on that amount would be about $876.53.

The mortgage tax is $0.115 per $100 of debt, with the first $2,000 exempt, and it falls on the borrower rather than the seller.

The tax is based on the greater of the price paid or the property's value, and the buyer swears to the figure on the deed in front of the register. A deed that cites a statutory exemption does not need that oath. Some transfers are exempt, including the creation or end of a tenancy by the entirety and the release of a life estate to the beneficiaries.

sections.h2: What makes the register accept or reject a Franklin County deed?
sections.html:
The register checks whether a document can be accepted for filing and leaves legal sufficiency to the attorney who prepared it. According to the University of Tennessee county advisory service, a deed has to satisfy these points.

  • Legibility and a proper acknowledgment before a notary (T.C.A. 66-24-101 and 66-22-101)
  • Owner and taxpayer names with addresses (66-24-114)
  • A derivation clause naming the earlier recorded deed (66-24-110)
  • Preparer name and address (66-24-115)
  • Parcel identification number (66-24-122)
  • Fees and any tax due at the time of filing

A deed that is not in English needs a translation attached, and registers may refuse an unreadable document. A single missing item is enough to send the deed back, which can push a closing date. Compare the parcel number on the deed with the one on your tax bill before anyone signs.

sections.h2: What is Franklin County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Franklin County sits on the eastern edge of Middle Tennessee along the Alabama line. It covers 576 square miles, of which 555 are land, and it climbs from the Nashville Basin over the Highland Rim and onto the Cumberland Plateau, a rise of about 1,300 feet. The county was organized in 1807 and named for Benjamin Franklin, and Winchester is the seat.

The county's own website lists the University of the South at Sewanee, Tims Ford Reservoir and State Park, and a manufacturing base tied to the automotive industry. Wikipedia adds that Nissan built a large engine plant at Decherd and that the Arnold Engineering Development Center lies partly in the county. Cowan, Decherd, Estill Springs, Sewanee, Huntland, Sherwood and Winchester are the communities named on the county site, and Interstate 24 gives access to Chattanooga.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts put numbers on the housing picture:

  • 45,579 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 6.6 percent from the 2020 base
  • 77.4 percent owner-occupied, with a median gross rent of $894
  • Median household income of $63,494 and a median home value of $236,900
  • 22.5 percent of residents are 65 or older
  • 323 building permits issued in 2025

Median household income here is below the $75,003 of neighboring Dickson County and the $88,456 of Fayette County in the same Census table.

sections.h2: How does property tax affect a seller in Franklin County?
sections.html:
The Tennessee Comptroller's schedule makes January 1 the assessment date and says current-year taxes are due on the first Monday of October, with the last day to pay without interest on February 28. March 1 is the delinquency date. The Franklin County Assessor states that the final assessment applies a classification percentage from the state constitution and the county commission sets the rate.

Under the Comptroller's tax calculation page, residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value. On a $236,900 house, the assessed value would be about $59,225, and the tax is that figure divided by 100 and multiplied by the rate. Ask the trustee for the current rate and balance.

An owner who disputes the appraisal first goes to the county board of equalization, which meets June 1 under the schedule. A homeowner who is 65 or older, or disabled, may qualify for state tax relief if 2025 income was $38,470 or less. Applications go to the trustee and are due 35 days after the delinquency date.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Franklin County, Tennessee?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds, 1 South Jefferson Street in Winchester, TN 37398. Call (931) 967-2840. The register is Nancy K. Ringer, and the office is in the county seat.

faqs.q: Who do I call to check my Franklin County property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Franklin County Trustee at (931) 967-2962. The trustee collects the tax, while the Property Assessor at (931) 967-3869 handles the appraisal and assessment.

faqs.q: How many parcels does the Franklin County assessor track?
faqs.a: About 25,000. The assessor keeps a property record card on each parcel, updated weekly through the state's Local Assessor System for web viewing.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Franklin County house worth $236,900?
faqs.a: About $876.53. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of the price or value, and the buyer pays it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Which communities are in Franklin County, Tennessee?
faqs.a: The county website names Cowan, Decherd, Estill Springs, Sewanee, Huntland, Sherwood and Winchester, with Winchester as the county seat. Sewanee is home to the University of the South.
